summary: Both regressions are fixed; the full gate is blocked by one out-of-scope test that asserts the old approximation.
body:
May I update `crates/interchange/src/scene/import/tests.rs::scene_import_css_bezier_and_local_keys_under_group_clock`? Your scope restriction requires approval before editing it. Its expected two approximate EaseIn keys must become 26 baked linear keys spanning media time 0–2s, with a baking report. The file remains untouched.

Files changed:

- `crates/interchange/src/scene/export.rs`
- `crates/interchange/src/scene/export/tests.rs`
- `crates/interchange/src/scene/import/properties.rs`
- `crates/interchange/tests/scene_roundtrip.rs`

Public API is unchanged:

```rust
pub fn import_with(bytes: &[u8], format: Format, opts: &ImportOptions) -> Result<(Imported, Report)>
pub fn export(project: &Project, sequence: ItemId, format: Format, opts: &ExportOptions) -> Result<(Vec<u8>, Report)>
```

Design: intrinsic Motion/Opacity keys now convert media ticks to local ticks using checked rational speed math, including the reverse endpoint’s −1 tick. The XSD’s `keyType@time` allows signed doubles without layer-interval bounds, so outside keys survive. Reversed hold discontinuities use adjacent local ticks and report the boundary bake. FilmCraft’s fixed-slope temporal handles represent compatible CSS curves exactly; other curves receive bounded frame-rate baking. Motion axis merging preserves influences or reports baking when independent curves require it. Semantics follow `scene-render.xsd` (`keyType`, `animateType@timeBase`) and `crates/project/src/keyframe.rs::ease`.

Borrowed/adapted semantics: temporal-handle conversion and named CSS control points from `/home/admin/src/scene-render/crates/sr-eval/src/curve.rs::resolve`. The integrator should record that source in attribution; no attribution files were edited.

TDD red→green evidence:

- `filmcraft_trimmed_speed_opacity_ease`: first key restored at 6s instead of 2s → passes.
- `filmcraft_opacity_ease_curve`: 26.5625 instead of 29.375 → passes.
- `scene_export_media_keys_speed_two`: exported 6s/8s instead of 1s/2s → passes.
- `scene_export_media_keys_reverse_and_outside`: wrong media timestamps instead of local −1s/5s → passes.
- `scene_import_named_ease_quarters` and `scene_import_css_baked_frame_values`: failed 1e-6 value assertions → pass.
- `filmcraft_all_eases_at_frames_forward_and_reverse`: exposed reversed Bezier handles and hold-boundary errors → all seven interpolations pass every tested frame.
- `scene_import_motion_css_handles`: x=15.625 instead of 12.9161931047 → passes.

Updated existing expectation: `scene_export_inexact_source_and_animation` now expects local zero for a key at the in-point, and two inexact timestamps instead of three.

Final VM results:

- Clippy with `--all-targets -- -D warnings`: PASS.
- Unfiltered gate: **FAIL**, 212 unit tests passed; only the legacy approximation assertion failed.
- Complete test run filtering that assertion: **296 passed**, including all 25 round-trip tests and remaining S5/S6 tests.
- `cargo xtask wasm`: PASS.

Both regressions remain unignored. No local builds, new dependencies, commits, or pushes. Only the four listed files changed; no locks are held.
